subject: Post-call: CloudFin + Redwood integration recap & next steps

Subject: Post-call: CloudFin + Redwood integration recap & next steps

Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum.

Key pain points you shared:
- Search relevance deteriorates at scale; current reranking pipeline is adding 2-3x latency and costs are spiking with embeddings.
- Need sub-200ms p99 latency for our assisted workflows.
- Desire to call internal APIs (user/profile store) to enrich responses (structured output + function-calling).
- Concern about SDK changes and migration effort for our client apps.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Proof-of-concept: reduce end-to-end query latency and cost for reranking use case.
2) Implement function-calling for deterministic DB lookups and return structured JSON to the UI.
3) Evaluate streaming for faster perceived response times on long responses.
4) Measure unit economics (tokens/second, infra cost) for hosted vs dedicated.

Product fit / technical notes (high level):
- SDK: lightweight client updates (2 small surface changes) — streaming and function-call wrappers. Backwards compatible.
- Function calling: Redwood supports typed function schemas; we can map your profile lookup and transaction_summary functions to those.
- Streaming: we can enable streaming on the route to push tokens as they’re generated (reduces time-to-first-byte).
- Embeddings & reranking: recommend offline embedding store + in-request lightweight rerank using short-listing + model-based reranker to save token spend.

Attachments: integration-mvp-sow.pdf (draft timeline & milestones), redwood-feature-matrix.xlsx (capabilities mapping).

Next steps (proposed):
- Jordan to run a 30-min technical deep-dive next week to walk SDK changes + function-calling mapping. (Jordan: can you share availability?)
- We’ll provision a sandbox account and push a sample integration (small repo + sample prompts) for you to test.
- Alex/Priya: please share 1-2 representative queries and a small sample of documents (anonymized) so we can baseline latency & relevance.
- Marissa to send an updated SOW and rough pricing bands for hosted vs dedicated.

If that looks right I’ll schedule the technical call and loop in CS for onboarding.

Thanks,

Hey Alex — quick technical answers and proposed plan: 

SDK changes
- Surface additions: (1) StreamClient wrapper (opt-in), (2) function_calling schema helpers. Both are thin and backward compatible; existing call patterns work unchanged if you don’t opt in.
- Migration effort: ~1-2 developer days to update web clients to the new helper functions; mobile may need a bit more depending on platform but we provide sample clients.

Function calling & auth
- We recommend a proxy pattern: Redwood issues short-lived, scoped tokens for the proxy service. The proxy then calls your internal APIs using service credentials. This avoids embedding long-lived secrets in the client.

Streaming & structured outputs
- Streaming is simply enabling chunked responses over the same route. UI change is minimal (switch from single response render to progressive append).
- For structured outputs we’ll use typed function responses so you get deterministic JSON back — easy to validate on the client.

Embeddings / reranking design (high level)
1) Indexing: produce embeddings offline and store in FAISS/managed vector store.
2) Shortlist: use a cheap ANN lookup to produce candidates.
3) Rerank: call a compact reranker model (lower tokens) on the shortlist to reorder. This saves tokens vs full-generation rerank attempts.

Proposed immediate actions
- I’ll provision the sandbox and push sample repo (redwood/examples/cloudfin-rerank) by EOD today.
- Schedule a 30-min tech call next week to walk through code and perform a quick live run.
- Share a short checklist for sample data format (CSV + doc snippets).

Sample code snippet (Node.js):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
// function call example
const res = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-reranker-v1',
  function_call: { name: 'profile_lookup', parameters: { user_id: '12345' } }
});

Happy to go deeper on any of these points on the tech call.

—Jordan
